notes: Accept. 180 items, 178 missing and 2 planned, every missing item routed exactly once across eight routes. I reproduced the recorded hash of arXiv v4 (1e4b6720…). All stages named by the six source routes exist in data/atlas.json; both proposed areas (ktheory, algebraicnt) are galaxy ids; the Part II's title reproduces its parent's atlas title exactly; and the two planned items name ArithmeticKTheory layers that exist. The five findings are all printed exactly as quoted and correctly diagnosed. E2 is the one reaching a stated result and it holds: Proposition 1.3.1 is stated for a general stable ∞-category C ('Let C be a stable ∞-category with a bounded t-structure … Let Q be an r-symmetric Poincaré structure on C with duality D: C → C^op') and its conclusion is about L^{a,b}_n(C,Q) → L_n(C,Q), but parts (i) and (ii) both write P_n(D^p(R), Q^{[−n]}) for a ring R the hypotheses never introduce. E5 is a genuine logical gap — not dividing the discriminant gives unramifiedness, not inertia, and the extraction's own counterexample, Q(√−7), settles it; the conclusion happens to be true for the Eisenstein integers, which is why it is recorded as a gap and not an error. E1 ('when n ≤ 2n − 3'), E3 ('Using Remark 1.1.6' for a statement printed as '1.1.6. Lemma') and E4 (the kernel generator ⟨1,−2⟩ for ⟨1,−3⟩) are quoted verbatim. Of the 141 locator checks I could run, 136 land on exactly the page given; four were one page out and are corrected in place (Example 1.2.35 and Example 1.3.7 with Corollary 1.3.8 sit at the tops of pp. 27 and 30 rather than on 26 and 29; Remark 3.1.8 is on p. 52, not 53), and the fifth is the second page of Example 2.3.14, which spans pp. 46–47 exactly as the two findings on it say. Nothing was rejected and no item was deleted.
